items.title: Section 301 Turns on Another Country's Payment Rails — the Brazil Action
kv: USTR/Executive Office of the President · Notice

A Presidential Memorandum of Jul 15 (FR Doc. 2026-14654, published Jul 20) directs Trade Act section 301 action on Brazil's acts, policies and practices related to Digital Trade and Electronic Payment Services, alongside tariffs, intellectual property, ethanol and deforestation. USTR's companion Notice of Action published the same day (FR Doc. 2026-14542, 91 FR 45516). Read plainly: American trade coercion is now pointed at a foreign country's national electronic payment system. Pix is a sovereign rail; section 301 is the lever.

items.title: FedNow's Third Birthday — 1,800 Banks, $271B a Quarter, and a Ceiling Raised Twentyfold
kv: Fed360's anniversary item puts numbers on the public rail: 1,800+ live institutions, up from about 1,600 in January; seven of the ten largest U.S. banks aboard; Q1 2026 volume 2.7 million transactions worth $271.3 billion; reach claimed at over half of all American checking and savings accounts. The line worth keeping is the ceiling: launched at $500,000, lifted to $1 million in March 2025, lifted again to $10 million in November 2025. A retail instant-payments service does not need a ten-million-dollar transaction limit. That is a wholesale rail wearing a consumer coat.

items.title: Logan Calls for FOMC to Voluntarily Centrally Clear Its Operations
kv: Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas — Lorie Logan · Speech

At the NY Fed Future of Market Liquidity workshop, Dallas President Lorie Logan called for the FOMC to voluntarily centrally clear its open market operations (Treasury buys/sells and repo), even though the SEC clearing mandate does not apply to the Fed. Also flagged blockchain potential to integrate market segments and speed collateral flow. Extends her September 2025 TGCR proposal and April 2026 liquidity blueprint — the Fed re-plumbing itself onto the new infrastructure.

items.title: FedNow at Three — the Fed Lays ISO 20022 Track Toward Cross-Border, and Sits Down With the Private Clearing House
kv: Chief FedNow Executive Nick Stanescu's three-year Q&A names four things coming to the Fed's own instant rail: FedACH payee-name verification exposed to FedNow users by API; enhanced ISO 20022 message formats 'that will lay the groundwork for the FedNow Service to enable cross-border payments'; a request-for-payment pilot; and Federal Reserve Financial Services co-chairing a newly established X9 Fraud Forum jointly with The Clearing House. Read the last one twice. The Clearing House is the private rail owned by the biggest banks — RTP, the thing FedNow was built to compete with — and the Fed is now its co-chair on a shared standards body. The public rail and the incumbents' rail write the fraud rulebook together. Same absorption grammar as Cede & Co. surviving the DTC rewrite and Visa/Mastercard keeping their own book.

items.title: CFTC RFC: 24/7 Trading of Standard Futures and Perpetual Contracts
kv: Commodity Futures Trading Commission · Proposed Rule

The CFTC asks how US futures markets could run around the clock — and says the quiet part in Questions 7-9: how does margin settle 'when traditional payment systems such as Fedwire and CHIPS do not operate,' and what 'stablecoin or other tokenized settlement asset' fills the gap? A federal agency, in the Federal Register, admitting the dollar's official rails sleep and asking private tokens to work the night shift.

items.title: KC Fed Frames Kraken Account as Payment-Account Pilot
kv: Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City · Supplemental Disclosure

The Kansas City Fed published a supplemental document framing the Kraken Financial limited-purpose account (granted March 4, 2026) as a pilot of the Reserve Bank payment-account concept — the first live test of the prototype the Board proposed in FR 2026-10375. Only overdraft-rejecting services (Fedwire Funds) are available; neither the Kraken exchange nor other Payward subsidiaries get access. The pilot generates real-world data for the payment-account rulebook whose comment period closes July 27, 2026.

items.title: Standing Repo Facility — Aggregate Limit Removed, Full Allotment (FedTrade Plus)
kv: Federal Reserve Bank of New York · Operating Policy Statement

The Desk removes the aggregate operational limit on standing overnight repo operations and moves them to a full-allotment format on the new FedTrade Plus platform (one proposition per security type per operation, $40B max each). The Fed's overnight dollar backstop, formerly capped, is now effectively unlimited — and rebuilt on new rails. Announced Dec 10, effective Dec 11, 2025; a companion note flags a move toward central clearing of the facility.

items.title: Request for Information on Potential Actions To Address Payments Fraud
kv: Treasury Department — Comptroller of the Currency · Notice

The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC), Treasury; the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System (Board); and the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) seek public input on questions related to payments fraud. This request for information (RFI) offers the opportunity for interested stakeholders to identify ways that the OCC, the Federal Reserve System (FRS), and the FDIC could take actions collectively or independently in their varying respective roles to help consumers, businesses, and financial institutions mitigate check, automated clearing house (ACH), wire, and instant payments fraud.

items.title: Standing Repo Facility — Morning Operation Added (BNY Tri-Party)
kv: Federal Reserve Bank of New York · Operating Policy Statement

Adds a daily early-morning (8:15–8:30am ET) standing repo operation alongside the existing 1:30pm one, settling on the BNY tri-party platform, then still under the $500B combined cap. Effective June 26, 2025 — the step that preceded December's uncapping: the Desk re-timing and re-plumbing the repo backstop through 2025.

items.title: Project Pine: the Fed Pre-Builds a Tokenized Control Panel

The New York Innovation Center and BIS publish a prototype toolkit showing a central bank can run open-market operations, standing facilities, and emergency interventions as programmable smart contracts in a tokenized wholesale market — and can spin up new facilities 'easily and quickly.' The Fed's overnight dollar backstop, formerly capped, is now effectively unlimited — and rebuilt on new rails. Announced Dec 10, effective Dec 11, 2025; a companion note flags a move toward central clearing of the facility.

cells: Federal Reserve System · Notice
rails

The Board announces Fedwire Funds Service hours will expand to 22 hours/day, 6 days/week (Sunday–Friday), with National Settlement Service tracking it — an interim step toward round-the-clock 22x7x365 settlement, implementation expected 2028–2029. The wholesale dollar plumbing moving toward always-on, to defend the dollar's global role.

The Fiscal Service enables FedNow for federal agency payouts — eight-plus agencies live, FEMA pushing disaster money instantly instead of mailing checks. The state itself now pays citizens over the Fed's instant rail: Treasury and Fed plumbing fused at the retail edge, the completion of the EO 14247 arc.

Treasury announces an exchange-stabilization operation in Argentine pesos through the Exchange Stabilization Fund — the same statutory pocket that holds the gold certificates and sits ready for any revaluation play. The quiet fund is awake and working.

record.title: Fed Board Approves Fedwire and NSS Operation on Sundays and Holidays (22x6)
cells: Federal Reserve Board · Press Release
rails

The Board formally decides the central bank's settlement day will no longer respect the weekend — Fedwire and the National Settlement Service expand to Sundays and holidays, implementation no earlier than 2028, with full seven-day operation left on the table. The precondition for 24x7 markets settling in central-bank money.

record.title: FedNow Transaction Limit Raised Tenfold, to $10 Million
cells: Federal Reserve Financial Services · Press Release
rails

The instant-payment rail's cap jumps from $1 million to $10 million (effective November 12). With the average payment already past $100,000, FedNow stops being a retail toy and becomes a wholesale-adjacent rail.

record.title: Fedwire Completes the ISO 20022 Migration in One Cutover
cells: Federal Reserve Financial Services · Announcement
rails

The $4.7-trillion-a-day wire system cuts over to the global structured-data standard in a single shot, no coexistence with the legacy format. The dollar's main artery now speaks the same machine language as every payment system on earth — richer data for programmability, screening, and interop with tokenized rails.

record.title: Request for Information on Potential Actions To Address Payments Fraud
cells: Treasury Department — Comptroller of the Currency · Notice
rails

The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC), Treasury; the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System (Board); and the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) seek public input on questions related to payments fraud. This request for information (RFI) offers the opportunity for interested stakeholders to identify ways that the OCC, the Federal Reserve System (FRS), and the FDIC could take actions collectively or independently in their varying respective roles to help consumers, businesses, and financial institutions mitigate check, automated clearing house (ACH), wire, and instant payments fraud.

record.title: Standing Repo Facility — Morning Operation Added (BNY Tri-Party)
cells: Federal Reserve Bank of New York · Operating Policy Statement
rails

Adds a daily early-morning (8:15–8:30am ET) standing repo operation alongside the existing 1:30pm one, settling on the BNY tri-party platform, then still under the $500B combined cap. Effective June 26, 2025 — the step that preceded December's uncapping: the Desk re-timing and re-plumbing the repo backstop through 2025.

record.title: Project Pine: the Fed Pre-Builds a Tokenized Control Panel
cells: Federal Reserve Bank of New York · Report
rails

The New York Innovation Center and BIS publish a prototype toolkit showing a central bank can run open-market operations, standing facilities, and emergency interventions as programmable smart contracts in a tokenized wholesale market — and can spin up new facilities 'easily and quickly.' Published four months after the retail-CBDC ban; framed strictly as wholesale and hypothetical.
